mainTopic: The name of the שמחת בית השואבה, whether the חליל overrides שבת, and the dispute over wooden כלי שרת
overview: The גמרא first records a dispute over the celebration's name: is it שואבה ('drawing') or חשובה ('significant')? מר זוטרא says both versions are correct, and each one reflects a true feature of the celebration. Next comes a ברייתא: רבי יוסי בר יהודה says the חליל overrides שבת, and חכמים say it does not even override יום טוב. רב יוסף explains that they argue about the שיר של קרבן, and the root question is whether the main part of Temple song is the instrument or the voice. Everyone agrees that the music of the שמחת בית השואבה is only rejoicing and does not override שבת. רב יוסף tries to prove his explanation from a dispute about wooden כלי שרת, which he links to משה's wooden flute. The גמרא rejects the proof in two ways. First, the vessel dispute may be about whether we learn a normal case from a case with no choice (דנין אפשר משאי אפשר). Second, it may be about how to read the verse about the מנורה, using כלל ופרט וכלל or ריבוי ומיעוט. The עמוד ends as רב פפא begins a statement that continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Two versions of the celebration's name
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה and רב עינא disagree about the wording of the משנה. One reads שואבה and the other reads חשובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב יהודה and רב עינא disagree. One teaches 'שואבה' (drawing), and one teaches 'חשובה' (significant).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a disagreement about how to read one word in the משנה's name for the celebration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a question about the wording of the text, not about a law. One version calls it the 'celebration of drawing,' and the other calls it the 'significant celebration.' The two words sound alike in Hebrew, which is why the versions differ.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (introduces a statement by אמוראים)

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was stated:
Rav Yehuda and Rav Eina (disagreed),
one teaches: 'sho'eva' (drawing),
and one teaches: 'chashuva' (significant).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are two readings of the celebration's name: שואבה or חשובה.

steps.title: Both names are correct
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא says neither version is a mistake. שואבה comes from a פסוק about drawing water, and חשובה comes from רב נחמן's teaching that it is an important מצוה dating back to the six days of Creation.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: The one who reads שואבה is not mistaken, and the one who reads חשובה is not mistaken. שואבה is right, because it is written, 'And you shall draw water with joy.' חשובה is right, because רב נחמן said: It is an important מצוה, and it comes from the six days of Creation.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא settles the name question by showing that both readings have a solid basis.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each name highlights a different side of the celebration. שואבה points to the water-drawing for ניסוך המים, based on the פסוק in ישעיה. חשובה points to how important this מצוה is, since its roots go back to Creation.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And you shall draw water with joy' (ישעיה יב:ג)

steps.whatToRemember: Both names are valid. שואבה reflects the water-drawing, and חשובה reflects the special importance of the מצוה.

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said:
the one who teaches 'sho'eva' is not mistaken,
and the one who teaches 'chashuva' is not mistaken.
The one who teaches 'sho'eva' is not mistaken,
as it is written: 'And you shall draw water with joy.'
And the one who teaches 'chashuva' is not mistaken,
as Rav Nachman said:
it is a significant מצוה,
and it comes from the six days of Creation.
phrases.notes: The שיתין (channels under the מזבח for the libations) were made at Creation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the dispute over the name from step 1
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both readings are correct. Each one reflects a true feature of the celebration.

steps.title: Does the flute override Shabbat?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records a dispute. רבי יוסי בר יהודה says the חליל overrides שבת, and חכמים say it does not even override יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: The flute overrides שבת. These are the words of רבי יוסי בר יהודה. The חכמים say: It does not even override יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic by quoting a ברייתא that argues about whether flute-playing in the מקדש is allowed on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Playing an instrument is normally forbidden on שבת and יום טוב by rabbinic law. רבי יוסי בר יהודה allows it even on שבת. חכמים forbid it even on יום טוב, which is the more lenient day. The ברייתא does not say which kind of flute-playing it means, so the next step will explain that.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
the flute overrides Shabbat,
the words of Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda.
And the Sages say:
it does not override even a Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הֶחָלִיל דּוֹחֶה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: the חליל mentioned in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי בר יהודה says the חליל overrides שבת. חכמים say it does not even override יום טוב.

steps.title: The dispute is about the offering's song
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that the argument is about the music played with the קרבנות. It depends on whether the main part of שירה is the instrument or the voice.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: The dispute is about the song of the קרבן. רבי יוסי holds that the main part of song is the instrument, so it is part of the עבודה and overrides שבת. The Rabbis hold that the main part of song is the mouth, so the instruments are not עבודה and do not override שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף tells us which flute the ברייתא means and explains the reasoning behind each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something that counts as עבודה in the מקדש may be done on שבת. If the instruments are the main part of the Temple song, playing them is עבודה and is allowed. If the voice is the main part, the instruments are only an extra, so they are not עבודה and are not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: the song (by the לויים) that accompanied the offerings
the main part of song is the instrument
the main part of song is the mouth (voice)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the central question for the rest of this passage: is Temple music mainly instrumental or vocal?

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
the dispute is about the song of the offering,
for Rabbi Yosei holds:
the essence of song is with an instrument,
and it is (part of the) service, and it overrides Shabbat.
And the Rabbis hold:
the essence of song is with the mouth,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָאו עֲבוֹדָה הִיא, וְאֵינָהּ דּוֹחָה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת.
phrases.english: and it (the instrument) is not service, and does not override Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מַחְלוֹקֶת בְּשִׁיר שֶׁל קׇרְבָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains which case the ברייתא in step 3 is about and why the two sides disagree
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The flute dispute is about the קרבן song, and it depends on whether the main part of song is the instrument or the voice.

steps.title: The water-drawing song never overrides Shabbat
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees that the music at the שמחת בית השואבה is only rejoicing, so it does not override שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the song of the שואבה: everyone agrees it is rejoicing, and it does not override שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף adds that the flute at the water-drawing celebration is not part of the argument at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even רבי יוסי בר יהודה, who treats the קרבן music as עבודה, agrees that the שואבה music is just שמחה. Since it is not עבודה, it does not override שבת. This fits our משנה, which says the חליל is played on some days and not on others.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יוסי בר יהודה allows the שמחת בית השואבה flute on שבת. He only allows the flute that accompanies the קרבנות.

phrases.english: But the song of the Drawing (of water),
according to all, it is rejoicing,
and it does not override Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל שִׁיר שֶׁל שׁוֹאֵבָה, דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל שִׂמְחָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רב יוסף's explanation in step 4 to the קרבן song only
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone agrees the שואבה song is only שמחה and does not override שבת.

steps.title: רב יוסף brings a source about wooden vessels
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף supports his explanation with a ברייתא. רבי says wooden כלי שרת are invalid, and רבי יוסי בר יהודה says they are valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: From where do I say that they argue about this? It is taught in a ברייתא: Temple vessels that were made of wood, רבי says are invalid, and רבי יוסי בר יהודה says are valid.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף begins a proof by quoting another dispute that involves the same תנא, רבי יוסי בר יהודה. This step sets up the next move, where he will connect this dispute to Temple song.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first glance, this ברייתא has nothing to do with music. It is about what material Temple vessels may be made from. The connection will come in the next step.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
From where do I say that they disagree about this?
As it is taught (in a baraita):
service vessels that one made of wood,
Rabbi (Yehuda HaNasi) deems them unfit
and Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda deems them fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to support step 4
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's claim that רבי יוסי בר יהודה and the Rabbis argue over whether the main part of song is the instrument or the voice
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about wooden כלי שרת

steps.title: Connecting wooden vessels to משה's flute
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף suggests that the wooden-vessel dispute depends on the same question about song. If instruments are the main part, משה's wooden flute was a כלי שרת, and we can learn from it that wood is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it not that they argue about this? The one who says valid holds that the main part of song is the instrument, and we learn from משה's flute. The one who says invalid holds that the main part of song is the mouth, and we do not learn from משה's flute.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף finishes his proof by linking the vessel dispute to the instrument-versus-voice question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מקדש had a wooden reed flute from the time of משה. If instruments are the main part of the song, that flute was a real כלי שרת, so it shows that a כלי שרת may be made of wood. If the voice is the main part, the flute was not a כלי שרת, so we cannot learn anything about כלי שרת from it.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not that... (introduces a proposed inference)

phrases.english: What, is it not about this that they disagree?
The one who deems it fit holds:
the essence of song is with an instrument,
and we derive from the flute of Moses.
And the one who deems it unfit holds:
the essence of song is with the mouth,
and we do not derive from the flute of Moses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the ברייתא in step 6 proves step 4
steps.raayaObject: That the root of the dispute is instrument versus voice
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wooden-vessel dispute, understood through the status of משה's flute

steps.title: The vessel dispute may be about something else
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Perhaps everyone agrees that the main part of song is the instrument, and they argue only about whether we can learn a normal case from a case where there was no other choice.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone agrees that the main part of song is the instrument. Here they argue about whether we learn 'possible' from 'impossible.' The one who says valid holds that we do learn possible from impossible. The one who says invalid holds that we do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב יוסף's proof by offering a different reason for the wooden-vessel dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה's flute had to be made of wood, because a flute made of metal does not sound as good. Other vessels could easily be made of metal. So the real question may be whether a case where there was no choice can teach us about cases where there is a choice. If so, the vessel dispute does not prove that the two sides disagree about instruments versus voice.

keyTerms.meaning: we derive a case where there is a choice from a case where there was no choice

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף's proof is pushed aside. The wooden-vessel dispute can be explained by the rule of דנין אפשר משאי אפשר, so it does not prove a dispute about instruments versus voice.
steps.confusionAlert: The דחיה does not say רב יוסף's explanation of the flute dispute is wrong. It only says his proof is not conclusive.

phrases.english: No, everyone agrees:
the essence of song is with an instrument,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָכָא בְּדָנִין אֶפְשָׁר מִשֶּׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר קָמִיפַּלְגִי.
phrases.english: and here they disagree about whether one derives the possible from the impossible.
The one who deems it fit holds:
one derives the possible from the impossible,
and the one who deems it unfit holds:
one does not derive the possible from the impossible.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא עִיקַּר שִׁירָה בִּכְלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference made in step 7
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the wooden-vessel ברייתא, not רב יוסף's explanation itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The vessel dispute can be explained by a different principle, דנין אפשר משאי אפשר, without any disagreement about instruments versus voice.

steps.title: Another way to reject the proof: the argument is about how to read the verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers a second rejection. Everyone agrees that the main part of song is the voice, and that we cannot learn a normal case from a case with no other choice. The real argument is about which method to use when reading the verse about the מנורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you want, say this instead: everyone agrees that the main part of song is singing with the mouth. Also, we do not learn what is possible from what was impossible. Here they argue about how to learn the laws of the מנורה. Do we use 'general rules and details,' or 'inclusions and exclusions'? רבי uses general rules and details. רבי יוסי בר יהודה uses inclusions and exclusions.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to רב יוסף's proof. It says the wooden-vessel argument may have nothing to do with music at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 8, both sides agreed that the instrument is the main part of song. Now the גמרא says the opposite: both sides agree that the voice is the main part. If so, משה's flute was never a כלי שרת, so it proves nothing about wood. The argument is moved to a completely different topic: two methods of reading the verse about the מנורה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you want, say' – this introduces a second, different answer
The main part of song is the voice (the mouth), not the instrument
We do not learn a normal case from a case where there was no other choice
A method of reading verses that uses general rules and details
A method of reading verses that uses inclusions and exclusions

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this answer up with step 8. In step 8, both sides agreed that the INSTRUMENT is the main part. Here, both sides agree that the VOICE is the main part. These are two separate and opposite rejections of רב יוסף.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
that everyone agrees that the main part of song is with the mouth,
phrases.notes: So the flute is not a כלי שרת

phrases.english: and one does not learn the possible from the impossible,
and here, it is about deriving (the laws of) the candelabrum

phrases.aramaic: בִּכְלָלֵי וּפְרָטֵי אוֹ בְּרִבּוּיֵי וּמִיעוּטֵי קָא מִיפַּלְגִי.
phrases.english: whether by general rules and details or by inclusions and exclusions that they argue.
Rabbi interprets with general rules and details,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה דָּרֵישׁ רִיבּוּיֵי וּמִיעוּטֵי.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda interprets with inclusions and exclusions.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא דְּעִיקַּר שִׁירָה בַּפֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, opposite way of rejecting רב יוסף's proof (step 7). Step 8 already gave the first way.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: It rejects the whole link between the wooden-vessel argument and the question of song.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The wooden-vessel argument can be fully explained by two different methods of reading the verse, without any connection to whether the voice or the instrument is the main part of song.

steps.title: רבי's reading: the vessels must be made of metal
steps.stepSummary: רבי reads the מנורה verse as general rule, then detail, then general rule. So he includes only things that are like the detail, gold. That means metal only, and wood is not allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי uses general rules and details. 'And you shall make a מנורה' is a general rule. 'Of pure gold' is a detail. 'It shall be made of beaten work' is a general rule again. With a general rule, a detail, and a general rule, you include only things like the detail. The detail is clearly a metal, so everything must be made of metal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רבי reads the verse about the מנורה. This reading leads to his rule that wooden כלי שרת are not allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the rule of כלל ופרט וכלל, the general parts only add things that are similar to the detail. Gold is a metal, so only metals are allowed. Wood is not a metal, so it is excluded. The מנורה is used as the model for all the כלי שרת.

keyTerms.meaning: General rule, then detail, then general rule – include only things that are similar to the detail
Beaten (hammered) work, made from one solid piece

phrases.english: Rabbi interprets with general rules and details:
'And you shall make a candelabrum of' – a general rule,
'pure gold' – a detail,
'of beaten work shall the candelabrum be made' – it went back and made a general rule.
A general rule, a detail, and a general rule:

phrases.aramaic: אִי אַתָּה דָן אֶלָּא כְּעֵין הַפְּרָט.
phrases.english: you include only what is similar to the detail.
Just as the detail clearly states something of metal,
so too everything must be of metal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the first of the two reading methods named in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By using כלל ופרט וכלל, only metal vessels are allowed, so wooden כלי שרת are not allowed.

steps.title: רבי יוסי בר יהודה's reading: everything is included except earthenware
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר יהודה reads the same verse as inclusion, then exclusion, then inclusion. This includes almost everything, even wood, and excludes only earthenware.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר יהודה uses inclusions and exclusions. 'And you shall make a מנורה' includes. 'Of pure gold' excludes. 'It shall be made of beaten work' includes again. With inclusion, exclusion, and inclusion, everything is included. What did it include? Every material. What did it exclude? Earthenware.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רבי יוסי בר יהודה reads the same verse in a different way. This reading leads to his rule that wooden כלי שרת are allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With ריבה ומיעט וריבה, the inclusion is very wide. Only the thing least like the exclusion is left out. Gold is the finest material, and earthenware is the least respected material, so only earthenware is excluded. Wood is included. Now both sides of the argument in step 6 are explained without any connection to music.

keyTerms.meaning: Include, exclude, include – almost everything is included

steps.whatToRemember: In this second answer, the wooden-vessel argument is only about how to read the verse. רבי uses כלל ופרט, so only metal is allowed. רבי יוסי בר יהודה uses ריבוי ומיעוט, so everything except earthenware is allowed. Music is not part of this argument at all.
steps.confusionAlert: Both תנאים read the exact same verse. Only the reading method is different, and that is what changes the result.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה, דָּרֵישׁ רִיבּוּיֵי וּמִיעוּטֵי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda interprets with inclusions and exclusions:
'And you shall make a candelabrum of' – it included,
'pure gold' – it excluded,
'of beaten work shall the candelabrum be made' – it went back and included.
It included, excluded, and included – so it included everything.
What did it include? It included all materials,
what did it exclude? It excluded earthenware.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה, דָּרֵישׁ רִיבּוּיֵי וּמִיעוּטֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the second reading method from step 9, as the opposite of רבי's reading in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By using ריבה ומיעט וריבה, every material is allowed, including wood. Only earthenware is excluded.

steps.title: רב פפא begins a new statement
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא is introduced. His actual statement continues on the next עמוד.
steps.whatsHappening: This line is only a setup. The גמרא is introducing רב פפא, and his words come in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The discussion of the wooden vessels is now finished. רב פפא's statement will go back to רב יוסף's explanation, which said the argument about the flute depends on what role song plays in the קרבנות.

keyTerms.meaning: 'רב פפא said' – introduces a new statement by this אמורא

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
phrases.notes: His statement continues on the next עמוד

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the wooden-vessel discussion and returns to רב יוסף's explanation from step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not stated on this עמוד. It is only the opening attribution.
